core.title: Model each exchanged artifact as a theme-namespaced, URN-identified, location-mirroring unit
core.given: A plan, product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance or planning doc declares or references a unit product capabilities produce or consume (material, contract, schema).
core.when: The planner names or decomposes that exchanged unit.
core.then: Model it as an artifact: a domain unit naming WHAT is exchanged, URN-identified, theme-namespaced, following the stack's canonical artifact naming pattern, with identity mirroring its declared location.
prefer: Make the top segment of the URN a canonical theme.
Follow the canonical naming pattern's separator semantics for hierarchy and variant.
Make its identity mirror its declared location (physical or contract).
Reference it from the DESIRED OUTCOMES and acceptances that prove it.
avoid: Describing it as runtime flow variables in flight — a coder/tester concern.
Citing this definition as the enforcement point; the requiring rule nodes enforce it.
core.why: A stable shared meaning of 'artifact' lets product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES and acceptances agree on WHAT is exchanged; the enforceable parts live in the naming rules that require this definition.
evidence: Advisory semantic anchor: not itself bound to a validator; compliance is established transitively by the requiring naming-rule nodes.

Reviewer confirms the artifact is described as a produced/consumed domain unit (material, contract, schema) exchanged by product capabilities and proven by DESIRED_OUTCOMES/acceptances, not as runtime flow variables.
verification: Advisory definition: no detector or validator binds to this rule directly and it enforces nothing by itself; verifiers must instead evaluate the decomposed naming rules that require this definition.

Evaluation property map: artifact -> {urn-identified, theme-namespaced, naming-patterned, location-mirroring}; each property is verified by the naming rule that owns it, not by this definition. The naming pattern and its separator semantics come from the profile; how a file is recognized as one of the activation kinds comes from the profile's role assignment; per-rule severity, detector and finding ids are realization details of the requiring rules.

profileRequirements.meaning: Enumeration of the concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role and whose declarations or references of exchanged units activate this definition — the core's file_kind activation values. It says nothing about how a file is recognized as one of these kinds; that assignment comes from roles.assignment.
profileRequirements.bunValue: plan, product capability, desired outcome, acceptance, planning_doc, contract, schema

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file is assigned to one of those kinds, and thus into this definition's scope: the kind is derived from the file's path and extension; in particular the planning_doc kind is restricted to documentation under the planning area (e.g. markdown docs alongside plans and product capabilities) that defines exchanged artifacts — not arbitrary documentation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: file kind derived from path / extension; planning_doc = documentation files under the planning area (e.g. markdown docs alongside plans/capabilities) that define exchanged artifacts

profileRequirements.meaning: The canonical naming pattern that an exchanged artifact (material, contract, schema) must follow, including its hierarchy/variant separator semantics — the concrete content of the core's 'naming-patterned' property and of the 'canonical artifact naming pattern' in the obligation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant (colon for hierarchy, dot for variant)

neutralityNotes: This rule is an advisory semantic anchor, so the core keeps its definitional, non-enforcing nature and pushes all enforcement to the requiring naming rules. All sibling rule-id references (the planner.artifact-naming.* family, including the prefer-list short-id shorthand) are Bun realization details (bunOnly); the core's doesNotFire[2] correspondingly says 'the naming rules that require this definition' instead of naming the Bun family. The concrete naming pattern 'theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant' with colon/dot separators is carried by the proposed profile key urn.artifact, so the core's obligation restores exactly when instantiated with the Bun profile. Method vocabulary that is shared across stacks via the profile vocabulary (product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, theme, acceptance, planning doc, material/contract/schema) is kept in the core; it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path. How a file is recognized as one of the activation kinds travels with the profile: the kind enumeration in roles.plan_artifact.kinds (enumeration only) and the path/extension assignment — including the restriction of planning_doc to planning-area documentation that defines exchanged artifacts, not arbitrary documentation — in roles.assignment. bun.json states no concrete planning-area root or file suffixes, so no location or suffix key is instantiated; the recognition text is carried whole by roles.assignment.
